metadata.hardware_requirements: NVIDIA Quadro K620 GPU and Intel Xeon CPU E5-1650 (3.6 GHz, 6 cores)

nodes_source.source_quote: In this work, we propose a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) method to explore the potential of traffic video data in improving the efficiency of ramp metering.
nodes_source.description: Video frames from a controlled traffic area, preprocessed into position matrices, used as high-dimensional visual inputs for the DRL method.
nodes_source.reproducibility_rationale: Available from the corresponding author upon request.

nodes_source.source_quote: The simulation parameters regarding driving behaviors are calibrated based on empirical data.
nodes_source.description: Data used to calibrate driving behavior parameters for the SUMO microscopic traffic simulator.
nodes_source.reproducibility_rationale: Available from the corresponding author upon request.

nodes_process.node_name: Vehicle location extraction from video frames
nodes_process.source_quote: Vehicle locations are extracted from the traffic video frames and are reformed as position matrices.
nodes_process.description: This step extracts the (x, y) coordinates of individual vehicles from raw traffic video frames. These locations serve as the basis for further traffic state representation.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, tools required are generic but not named, no parameters stated.

nodes_process.node_name: Form position matrices from vehicle locations
nodes_process.source_quote: traffic state at time step t is represented by a position matrix m_t in R^X*Y; m_t(x, y) = U_v, i in I_t, where U_v is a constant and I_t refers to the set of vehicles in the control area at time step t.
nodes_process.description: Vehicle locations are reformed into a position matrix m_t of size X x Y. Vehicle positions are represented by a constant U_v, and signal states by U_G (green) or U_R (red) at specific coordinates (X_R, Y_R). All other matrix elements are set to zero.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, no tools named, parameters mentioned but values not stated.

nodes_process.source_quote: For computation efficiency, down-sampling is introduced before the matrix stack to reduce the input dimensions and maintain sufficient information about vehicle positions.
nodes_process.description: The position matrices are down-sampled to reduce the input dimensions, which helps in computational efficiency for subsequent steps while aiming to preserve essential vehicle position information.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=2, no tools named, no parameters stated.

nodes_process.source_quote: we stack the matrices of consecutive N time steps to represent the state s_t: S_t = {m_t-(N-1),..., m_t}.
nodes_process.description: To capture vehicle dynamics, the traffic state s_t is represented by stacking N consecutive down-sampled position matrices. This forms a sequence of observations as input for the DRL method.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, no tools named, 1/1 parameter stated.

nodes_process.source_quote: The reward r_t after action a_t is defined by the following: r_t = mu*v_t + omega*q_t, mu > 0, omega < 0
nodes_process.description: The reward function r_t for the DRL agent is defined as a linear combination of the average speed (v_t) in the merging area and the average queue length (q_t) at the on-ramp, weighted by mu and omega respectively. This balances mobility and queue delays.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, no tools named, all parameters stated.

nodes_process.source_quote: The Q-network in Mnih et al. [30] is revised as Figure 7, which consists of three convolutional neural network (CNN) layers and one full connection (FC) layer for each output layer.
nodes_process.description: A deep Q-network architecture, adapted from Mnih et al. [30], is defined. It comprises three convolutional neural network (CNN) layers followed by fully connected (FC) layers. For multitask learning, the FC layer is extended to two output layers for Q-value and speed/queue prediction.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, generic tools required, specific architecture details in Figure 7, most parameters stated.

nodes_process.source_quote: The Q-network is trained in 10^6 training frames, and each scenario is evaluated in 20 simulation experiments.
nodes_process.description: The deep Q-network is trained using the Adam optimizer to minimize a combined loss function (L(w_i) = L1(w_i) + lambda*L2(w_i)). The training incorporates experience replay and a target network for stability, and a multitask learning strategy for efficiency. An epsilon-greedy strategy is used for action selection.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, most tools named or referenced, most parameters stated, discount_factor_gamma not explicitly stated.

nodes_process.node_name: Set up SUMO traffic simulation environment
nodes_process.source_quote: The proposed method is evaluated in SUMO, an open-source microscopic traffic simulator [31].
nodes_process.description: A microscopic traffic simulation environment is set up using SUMO. It models a freeway connecting Qingdao and Huangdao, including a one-lane on-ramp, a three-lane mainline, and a merging area. Speed limits are 80 km/h for the mainline and 40 km/h for the on-ramp. Driving behavior parameters are calibrated with empirical data.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, all tools named, all parameters stated.

nodes_process.source_quote: The PI-ALINEA method fixes the length of the green phase and determines the length of the red phase in the current signal cycle based on the length of the red phase in the previous cycle and the downstream occupancies in the previous and current cycles.
nodes_process.description: The PI-ALINEA method is implemented as a baseline for comparison. It calculates the ramp metering rate r_k for the k-th cycle based on the previous red phase length and current/previous downstream occupancies, aiming for a desired mainline occupancy. The green phase length is fixed.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, tool named, all parameters stated.

nodes_process.source_quote: each scenario is evaluated in 20 simulation experiments. The simulations for the training phase and each experiment are initialized with different random seeds.
nodes_process.description: Twenty simulation experiments are conducted for each of three scenarios: (1) no ramp metering control, (2) PI-ALINEA ramp metering, and (3) the proposed Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) method. Each simulation is initialized with a different random seed.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, no tools named, all parameters stated.

nodes_process.source_quote: Figure 9 presents the Q1 (25%), Q2 (50%), and Q3 (75%) of the travel times in the mainline for three scenarios.
nodes_process.description: The travel times in the mainline are evaluated and compared across the no-control, PI-ALINEA, and DRL scenarios. Results are presented as Q1, Q2, and Q3 percentiles, and mean travel times in a table.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, no tools named, all parameters stated.

nodes_process.source_quote: Figure 10 presents the temporal-spatial distribution of the mean speeds along the mainline.
nodes_process.description: The temporal-spatial distribution of mean speeds along the mainline is evaluated for the no-control, PI-ALINEA, and DRL scenarios. This provides insight into traffic flow efficiency.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, no tools named, no parameters stated.

nodes_process.source_quote: Figure 11 presents the Q1, Q2, and Q3 of the queue lengths at the on-ramp in three scenarios.
nodes_process.description: The queue lengths at the on-ramp are evaluated for the no-control, PI-ALINEA, and DRL scenarios, presented as Q1, Q2, and Q3 percentiles. The relationship between queue length and red ratios, and queue length and occupancy, are also analyzed.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, no tools named, all parameters stated.

nodes_process.source_quote: The better performance of the proposed DRL method is further revealed when considering traffic flows downstream of the merge area, which is demonstrated in Figure 14.
nodes_process.description: Traffic flows downstream of the merge area are evaluated and compared across the no-control, PI-ALINEA, and DRL scenarios. This assessment highlights the DRL method's effectiveness in alleviating capacity drop impacts.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, no tools named, no parameters stated.

nodes_process.source_quote: A perturbation analysis is conducted to evaluate the impact of information contained in video data. As shown in Figure 15, the control area is divided into eight subareas.
nodes_process.description: The control area is divided into eight subareas. For each subarea, information is removed from the original data to create perturbed datasets. These perturbed datasets are then used in 20 simulation experiments to analyze the impact of missing information on control performance.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, no tools named, all parameters stated.

nodes_process.node_name: Evaluate travel times with perturbed data
nodes_process.source_quote: Figure 16 presents the box plot of travel time when the information of different subareas is removed, and the baseline is the result of experiments that take original data as input.
nodes_process.description: Travel times are evaluated from simulations conducted with perturbed input data, where information from different subareas was removed. This analysis quantifies the impact of specific video data information on the DRL method's performance.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, no tools named, no parameters stated.
